api_analysis.hypothesis: The compile error is due to using the same name `sdata` for extern shared memory arrays of different types (float and int64_t) in two kernel templates within the same translation unit. CUDA/NVCC treats these as conflicting declarations because extern shared memory arrays with the same name but different types are not allowed in the same scope/file. The fix is to rename one of the shared memory arrays, e.g. use `sdata_count` in the count_nonzero kernel, while keeping the kernel logic unchanged.
evidence: Compile error at custom_ops.cu(119): declaration is incompatible with previous "sdata" (declared at line 64). Line 64 is inside unfold_amax_kernel which declares `extern __shared__ T sdata[];` (float), and line 119 is inside unfold_count_nonzero_kernel which declares `extern __shared__ int64_t sdata[];`.
NVCC does not allow multiple extern shared memory declarations with the same identifier but different types in the same translation unit.
The kernels themselves are logically correct; this is purely a naming conflict.
changes: In kernels/custom_ops.cu, rename the shared memory array in unfold_count_nonzero_kernel from `sdata` to `sdata_count` and update all references within that kernel.
No changes needed to binding, launcher signatures, or model_new.py.
After this change, compilation should proceed past this error; subsequent errors (if any) will be addressed based on new logs.
